# omada_access_point_port (Resource)

Manages the VLAN of one Ethernet (LAN) port on an adopted access point — the port an EAP passes a wired device through, such as `ETH2` on an EAP245. The VLAN is set by id, as the controller's *VLAN ID* option does; binding a port to a network profile, and tagged VLANs, are not modelled.

~> **The write is inferred, not confirmed on hardware.** The port's shape was read from a live controller; the write sends the body another Omada client sends. The AP is read back after every write: a VLAN the controller did not store, or any other port setting that moved, fails the apply. That proves what the controller stored, not that the AP applied it.

~> **A port is physical: it cannot be created or destroyed.** Terraform *adopts* the existing port. Removing this resource from your configuration leaves the port exactly as last applied — Terraform forgets it, the AP does not. Changing a port's VLAN moves whatever is plugged into it onto another network.

~> **The AP's uplink port is refused**: its VLAN carries the AP's own management traffic, so a wrong value there cuts the AP off from the controller. So is any port the AP does not report as VLAN-capable, and every port of an AP that does not report its uplink as fixed (`supportUplinkPortConfig` false). An EAP245 lists only `ETH2`, which is VLAN-capable, and has a fixed uplink.

Every settable attribute is optional: whatever you leave out keeps its current value on the controller, and will never report drift. The port is written only when a configured value differs from the device.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Put whatever is plugged into the AP's ETH2 (a TV, a printer) on the IoT
# network, untagged. The AP's uplink is never written.
#
# vlan_id, if set, needs vlan_enable = true; left out, it keeps the port's id.
resource "omada_access_point_port" "tv" {
  ap_mac = data.omada_devices.all.devices[0].mac
  port   = "ETH2"

  vlan_enable = true
  vlan_id     = omada_network.iot.vlan_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ap_mac` (String) MAC address of the access point, in any common spelling. See the `omada_devices` data source.
- `port` (String) The port's name as the controller reports it, e.g. `ETH2`.

### Optional

- `site` (String) Site name. Defaults to the primary site. Changing forces replacement.
- `vlan_enable` (Boolean) Put untagged traffic on this port into `vlan_id`. Off, the port carries whatever the AP's uplink carries untagged.
- `vlan_id` (Number) The VLAN untagged traffic on this port goes into when `vlan_enable` is on: the `vlan_id` of the `omada_network` the port should be on. Reads `0` on a port whose VLAN has never been set, so enabling one there needs this too. Requires `vlan_enable = true`: while the VLAN is off the id has no effect, and the controller may not keep it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<ap mac>/<port>`.
- `name` (String) The port's label in the controller. Read-only.
- `site_id` (String)
- `support_vlan` (Boolean) Whether this port's VLAN can be written, unless `uplink` is true: the port and the AP's list of VLAN-capable ports both say it can, and the AP's uplink is fixed (`supportUplinkPortConfig` false). Read-only.
- `uplink` (Boolean) Whether the controller marks this as the port the AP is connected through, on the port or in the AP's device details. Read-only; such a port is never written. An EAP245 does not list its uplink at all, so it cannot be managed here.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By "<ap mac>/<port>" (the primary site is assumed):
terraform import omada_access_point_port.tv 10-5A-95-89-C3-64/ETH2

# Or "<site>/<ap mac>/<port>" to name the site explicitly:
terraform import omada_access_point_port.tv Home/10-5A-95-89-C3-64/ETH2
```
